instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under § 13.63, and § 13.63(1)(a) provides for obtaining that license to practice lobbying.
A lobbyist license 'shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,' implying renewal on a biennial (24-month) cadence.
The law creates distinct requirements for lobbyists to be licensed (§ 13.63) and principals to register (§ 13.64), with separate written authorizations linking them (§ 13.65).
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from specified lobbying subchapter provisions when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under § 13.695 and named officials are not subject to several lobbying requirements, establishing a partial exemption for state agencies/officials.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The provided sections specify license application contents and expirations but do not state any general deadline for a lobbyist to amend/update a license application after changes.
The statute prohibits lobbying as a lobbyist unless already licensed and authorized (§ 13.66) but does not specify a numeric number of days after first lobbying in which registration must occur.
No provision in the provided licensing/registration sections (§§ 13.63-13.68, 13.75) mentions submitting a photograph with a lobbyist license application.
